svg.text: BOOT button = GPIO9, blue LED = GPIO8
ESP32-C3 SuperMini · 3.7" e-paper · WS2812B ring · rotary encoder · vibration motor
Same label = same wire. Match the pins by the names printed on each board; the order on yours may differ.
1. Power everything from the C3's USB-C. Keep LED brightness at or below 60 of 255 (the default): 12 LEDs at full white draw about 0.7 A.
2. The encoder's + pin goes to 3V3. Its pull-up resistors would put 5 V on the C3's pins, and the C3 only takes 3.3 V.
3. If the ring flickers or shows wrong colours, feed its 5V through a 1N4001 diode (4.3 V), so the C3's 3.3 V data counts as high.
4. GPIO9 is also the BOOT button: holding the knob down while plugging in starts the C3 in download mode (useful for flashing).
